opus.market_notes: Neon jump/slide auto-runner is one of the most saturated mobile lanes (Geometry Dash, Subway Surfers, Alto-likes). Nothing mechanically new here, so it would depend heavily on UA spend and polish to stand out.
opus.summary: This is a working prototype with a reasonable variable-jump, coyote-time and buffered-input loop. It has 14 stages that the bot confirms are clearable, a decent coherent AI-generated synthwave art pack, and passing tests. But the stages are tiny, about 6 to 38 hazards and roughly 10 seconds each, so the whole game lasts minutes. The HUD is cluttered and overlaps itself, as the smoke screenshot shows, and the audio is all procedural synth with no settings. There is nothing for monetization, privacy or the store beyond icons. It is not shippable today.
blockers: Content too thin: 14 stages of about 10 seconds each, with districts 7-14 reusing backdrops 1-6. There is no endless mode, no unlockables and no meta progression to keep players coming back.
No monetization, privacy policy, analytics/consent or store screenshots. The ads and IAP hooks don't exist at all, not even as stubs, and orientation is 'any' with no locked layout.

HUD and UX clutter. The NEXT/urgency/PB-pace/progress text overlaps the tutorial tip and the result panel (see smoke.png). Several HUD layers are separate IIFEs that poll DOM text every 100ms. There's no settings screen (mute, volume, haptics toggle).
Audio is all procedural WebAudio oscillators and noise, with no composed music or recorded SFX assets. Nobody has checked the mix on device.
There has been no device QA or real Capacitor build (no ios/android projects). The 2-3MB background PNGs aren't optimized, and the runner sprite reads very small against busy backgrounds.
